entries.name: Western Balkans / Bosnia & Kosovo
entries.reason: The Hague conviction of four former KLA leaders has triggered sustained protests and cross-party pushback in Kosovo, alongside a court-set October 6 deadline to elect a president or face snap elections. Honours paid in Serbia to Ratko Mladic have also drawn condemnation at the UN. Together these raise political strain modestly. There are no kinetic developments or RS referendum steps, and a Bosnian court curbed RS secessionist lobbying, so the core hypotheses and priority stand.

changes.why: The Kosovo verdict protests, the looming presidential deadline and the Mladic glorification row add political strain without kinetic escalation.

entries.name: Afghanistan
entries.reason: Direct Pakistan–Taliban fighting resumed on September 18 after a nearly three-month lull. It has continued into a second week, with Pakistani airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan, cross-border attacks, targeted operations and a car bombing. Pakistan has declared 'an open war', and analysts see little Taliban incentive to meet its demands. This is a clear escalation beyond the 'border frictions' in the current text. ACH is unchanged: external pressure does not yet discriminate between consolidation, IS-KP-driven crisis or internal split. The opium item [6] and the retrospective piece [5] are not material.

changes.why: Sustained interstate strikes and a declared 'open war' are a significant shift from border frictions.

entries.name: Venezuela Crisis
entries.reason: The reporting confirms an interim government under acting leader Delcy Rodríguez, her first meeting with President Trump, US removal of Venezuela from the drug blacklist, and releases of dozens of political prisoners. Priority stays at 3 because falling external pressure offsets higher humanitarian strain.

entries.name: Russia–Ukraine War
entries.reason: Russia has begun daytime jet-powered drone strikes on central Kyiv, and Ukrainian air defenses are reported to be struggling or running low. Separately, a US push for an energy ceasefire and trilateral talks has been reported, though Moscow publicly vows to continue the war. These support the attritional-campaign hypothesis and open a tentative diplomatic track, but do not justify moving the STI or priority. The Seoul–Kyiv POW dispute and other commentary are not material.
